question: How do the ṭa and ta classes arise from earlier phonetic conditions?
premises: From the limiting condition of the shadow of the repha part, linked to ṛ, arises the ṭa class.
From that same source, through dha, another sequence proceeds.
The progression follows the order of limiting shadow conditions.
inference: The ṭa and subsequent ta classes emerge through successive phonetic shadow conditions rooted in earlier sounds.
uncertainties: The exact phonetic derivation of dharāc in this chain is compressed and partly implicit.
plain_english: From that, through the limiting condition of the shadow of the repha part and from the letter ṛ, arises the ṭa class. From that again, through dha and by the sequence of limiting shadow conditions, the next class proceeds.
